findings.summary: The block journey still promises a block that lasts until the user removes it, which contradicts the new rule that a block lapses automatically after 90 days.
findings.evidence: J.control.block actorGoal: 'Stop all app-mediated contact from one person until I remove the block'; e1: 'Block in force until removed' vs entity.Block invariant 'Lapses automatically 90 days after creation'

findings.summary: Expiring blocks automatically takes control away from the blocker: after 90 days the blocked person can invite again, and the spec gives no way to renew or extend a block, which works against the autonomy and unwanted-pressure goals.
findings.evidence: 'A block prevents new app-mediated contact for 90 days, then lapses automatically'; C.webapp.revocation.current: 'A lapsed block restores invite eligibility'; P1: 'respecting both people's autonomy'; T4 outcome 'Less unwanted pressure'

findings.summary: S.webapp.prompts now limits goal suppression to 'until the block lapses', but no operation or scheduled effect lifts the pause or restores suggestions when a block lapses, so this behaviour has no mechanism.
findings.evidence: S.webapp.prompts: 'pause the blocker's corresponding goal and suppress its suggestions until the block lapses' vs operation.connection.revoke effects: 'Blocking pauses the blocker's corresponding goal' (no lapse handling; RelationshipGoal.pausedAt has no auto-clear)
